parameters.query:
-- Claim first, send second: followed_up_at is set in this statement, so a lead can never
-- be picked twice, even if two runs overlap or the send below fails.
UPDATE leads l SET followed_up_at = now(), followup_status = 'claimed', updated_at = now()
WHERE l.id IN (
  SELECT id FROM leads
  WHERE status = 'replied'
    AND followed_up_at IS NULL
    AND last_outbound_at < now() - ($1::numeric * interval '1 hour')
    AND last_inbound_at < last_outbound_at
  ORDER BY last_outbound_at
  LIMIT 20
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
RETURNING l.id AS lead_id, l.source, l.contact, l.contact_name,
  (now() - l.last_inbound_at) < interval '24 hours' AS in_window,
  (SELECT b.data->>'followup_message' FROM business_facts b WHERE b.id = 1) AS followup_message;

nodes.name: Send follow-up
nodes.notes: Sends the one follow-up text from business-facts.json.

parameters.query:
WITH d AS (SELECT $1::bigint AS id, $2::text AS action, $3::boolean AS sent)
, upd AS (
  UPDATE leads l SET
    status = CASE d.action WHEN 'send' THEN CASE WHEN d.sent THEN 'followed_up' ELSE 'needs_human' END
                           WHEN 'template_needed' THEN 'template_needed' ELSE 'followup_manual' END,
    followup_status = CASE WHEN d.action = 'send' AND NOT d.sent THEN 'send_failed' ELSE d.action END,
    last_outbound_at = CASE WHEN d.sent THEN now() ELSE l.last_outbound_at END,
    updated_at = now()
  FROM d WHERE l.id = d.id
  RETURNING l.id, l.status, l.contact, l.contact_name, l.source)
, msg AS (
  INSERT INTO lead_messages (lead_id, direction, channel, body, delivered)
  SELECT d.id, 'out', 'whatsapp', $4, true FROM d WHERE d.sent)
SELECT * FROM upd;

parameters.content:
## Follow-up
One follow-up per lead, ever: rows are claimed (`followed_up_at` set) before anything is sent.

WhatsApp free-form messages are only allowed within 24h of the customer's last message; outside it, status becomes `template_needed` and nothing is sent.
